title: Multistage LLM POC - Quantization Schedule & Prompt Cadence
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the experimental plan, early results, and an actionable rollout for a multistage conversational POC. Goal: demonstrate a production-friendly pipeline that balances latency, token cost, and answer quality for a customer-facing chat assistant (support + light knowledge retrieval). Focus areas: per-stage model selection, stagewise quantization, prompt cadence (how we split/chain prompts across stages), and token budgeting.

Customer context and constraints:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS with 10M annual queries, strict latency objective: 95th percentile < 650ms for single-turn retrieval+generate flows.
- Data: 250k support doc passages, vector index planned (FAISS) in same region.
- Privacy: cannot send raw customer data to hosted third-party models; must run on Dedicated or Private.
- Budgetary target: reduce per-response token compute cost by ~40% vs baseline (fp16 Llama-2-13B) while keeping subjective quality drop < 7%.

High-level multistage pipeline (chosen for POC):
1) Fast intent classifier (tiny encoder) to detect low-effort responses (FAQ, redirects).
2) Retriever + re-ranker (embedding-based, sparse filter + small decoder re-rank).
3) Generator: produce final answer with grounded context; fallback options to higher-capacity model when hallucination risk is detected.
4) Reranker/quality-check (compact model or heuristic) for final scoring and short polishing (templating).

Stagewise model candidates and rationale:
- Classifier: small encoder-only model (e.g., Llama-2-7B-int4 distilled encoder-only variant or Mistral-small) quantized aggressively (int8/4) — objective: <10ms inference on a T4-equivalent core.
- Retriever: cheapest possible; embeddings on CPU/GPU using 2x-quantized model (e.g., OpenEmbed-small int8).
- Re-ranker: 3B-class decoder in int8 (GPTQ where available). Provides semantic ordering with low latency and low cost.
- Generator (primary): Llama-2-13B quantized to int8 (LLM.int8() optimized path). For high-precision fallback: Llama-2-13B fp16 on dedicated GPU or Llama-2-70B-int8 with bigger instance for long answers when generator confidence is low.

Stagewise quantization strategy (novelty: "stagewise precision tuning"):
- Rationale: different stages tolerate different precision losses. Classifier and retriever can be low-precision; generator is quality-sensitive.
- Profiles to test in POC:
  * Profile A: classifier int4 (GPTQ), retriever int8, re-ranker int8, generator int8
  * Profile B: classifier int8, retriever int8, re-ranker int8, generator fp16 (baseline for quality)
  * Profile C: classifier int4, retriever int8, re-ranker int4, generator int8 + selective fp16 fallback for >2-turn contexts
  * Profile D: classifier int4, retriever int8, re-ranker int8, generator int8 with per-token KV cache stored in 16-bit to reduce drift (hybrid precision)
- Notes on quantization methods: prefer GPTQ for 4-bit where available; LLama-compatible per-channel symmetric quant works well for int8. For generator we will test both standard LLM.int8() and GPTQ-quantized variants to compare subjective quality.

Prompt cadence and chaining (how prompts move across stages):
- Intent classifier: short prompt (<64 tokens) with 8-shot examples; strict timebox of 10ms CPU budget.
- Retriever call: query = canonicalized user question + 1-2 context signals from classifier (intent tag). We truncation-token budget target = 32 tokens per query to reduce embedding cost.
- Re-ranker: single-shot re-rank prompt that takes top-8 passages and returns top-3 with a confidence score. Output schema: JSON-like lines (simpler parsing).
- Generator prompt template (primary): system instructions (customer voice + safety rules) -> condensed context (top-3 passages concatenated with separators and source ids) -> user message. Prompt length cap: 1024 tokens; we will test aggressive chunking (split passages and call multiple short generator passes to stitch answers) vs single long prompt.
- Polishing / rerank pass: short prompt to re-ranker model to verify no hallucination and adjust tone; if confidence < threshold then trigger fallback to higher-precision model.

Token budgeting and rough cost model (POC estimates):
- Average user question: 18 tokens. Retriever embedding call: 18 tokens -> embeddings cost minimal but vector search infra cost + ~0.5ms per call.
- Average context returned: 3 passages x 120 tokens = 360 tokens. Generator input prompt total = ~400 tokens; expected generator output average 140 tokens.
- Baseline cost (fp16 13B): compute cost unit = X (abstract) -> baseline per-response GPU-time 180ms.
- Target cost improvement: with int8 generator + int4 upstream, we expect 35-50% reduction in GPU time per response in our microbench (see experimental logs).

Experiment logs (summary of initial runs on dev infra):
- Setup: p4d-lite testbed (simulated customer dataset subset of 5k queries). Measured 95p latency across combined pipeline including retrieval.
- Profile A (int8 generator): 95p latency = 620ms (meets SLO), subjective quality delta vs fp16: -4.2% (human eval composite), hallucination rate +2%. Token throughput: +40% vs fp16.
- Profile B (fp16 generator): 95p latency = 980ms (missed SLO), quality: baseline.
- Profile C (selective fp16 fallback): 95p latency = 680ms, quality delta: -2.6%, fallback triggered on ~9% of queries, cost savings ~30%.
- Observations: classifier and re-ranker quantization to int4 has negligible impact on downstream quality but reduced latency noticeably for small models. GPTQ-int4 picked up occasional tokenization artifacts for numeric tables — need post-processing heuristics.

Example prompts and few-shot seeds used in tests (copyable):
- Intent classifier few-shot seeds: (examples lines)
  "Q: My invoice is wrong -> INTENT: billing_dispute"
  "Q: How do I reset 2FA? -> INTENT: account_security"
  "Q: I want to upgrade plan -> INTENT: plan_change"

- Re-ranker prompt sketch: 
  "You are a re-ranking assistant. Input: a list of passages with id and relevance score. Output: return top 3 ids and a confidence score out of 1. Example: [passage1,id1], [passage2,id2] -> id2,id1 confidence 0.92"

- Generator system instruction (short):
  "You are the product support assistant for AcmeCorp. Use helpful, concise language. Always cite up to 2 source passages by id. If you must guess, say 'I don't know'. Limit length to 180 tokens unless user asks to expand. Tone: professional friendly."

Quality metrics we will track in POC (with targets):
- Answer accuracy (ground-truth-based) >= 90% recall on labelled dev set
- Hallucination rate <= 5% of answers (human-eval)
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 650ms
- Cost improvement >= 35% vs fp16 baseline

Rollout and gating checklist for customer demo:
- [ ] Run 10k query sweep with Profile A and Profile C; collect human evals across 200 diverse queries
- [ ] Add numeric-table post-processing to strip GPTQ artifacts (regex-based) and re-evaluate
- [ ] Implement KV-cache warmup strategy for multi-turn sessions (store per-session kvs in 16-bit)
- [ ] Instrument detailed per-stage metrics in Redwood Console (token-level cost, per-model latency, fallback counts)
- [ ] Prepare dashboard showing cost/latency/quality tradeoff curve to present in demo

Known risks and mitigations:
- GPTQ 4-bit artifacts with structured numeric content: mitigate via pre/post-processing; fall back to re-ranker heuristics for numeric extracts.
- Privacy constraint: some quantization toolchains require model access that is restricted in customer private environment. Mitigation: run quantization workflow in customer-controlled infra using our containerized GPTQ tool published in GH PR (linked).
- Fallback thrash: excessive fallbacks will negate cost savings. Mitigation: tune fallback thresholds with small live ramp and synthetic stress tests.

Decision log (quick):
- 2024-11-06: Chose Llama-2-13B as generator baseline for customer due to deterministic behavior and available quantized toolchain. (A.M.)
- 2024-11-08: Opted for selective fp16 fallback rather than always using fp16 for generator to meet latency SLO. (D.P.)
- 2024-11-15: Added post-processing step for GPTQ numeric artifacts after initial human eval flagged edge cases. (R.S.)

Next steps for POC (2-week sprint):
- Week 1: run 10k query sweep for Profiles A/B/C; implement numeric post-processing; add instrumentation for fallback reasons.
- Week 2: customer-facing demo build, run demo script with 50 synthetic queries, prepare executive summary including cost model and recommended Dedicated capacity sizing (anticipated: 4 x A10-like nodes for 95p SLO at 10qps baseline).

Appendix: quick config snippets used in benchmarking (copyable shell-like):
- Quantization command (GPTQ sketch):
  python gptq.py --model l2-13b --bits 4 --group-size 128 --out ./quantized/l2-13b-gptq4

- Generator runtime flags used on Redwood Dedicated testbed:
  --model quantized/l2-13b-gptq8 --batch-size 1 --max-new-tokens 180 --kv-cache true --sample-method greedy --temperature 0.0

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep human eval rubric simple: factuality / helpfulness / tone. 1-5 scale each.
- Check with infra team about spot vs reserved capacity for demo window (costs spike if fallbacks frequent).

If you want I can split this doc into two follow-ups: (1) a condensed one-pager to send to the customer and (2) a runbook with exact experiment commands, Docker images, and Jenkins job links.
